title: Excel / Spreadsheet Modelling
description: Build robust models in the most-used analytics tool in business. Tests pivot tables, what-if analysis, and simulation techniques.

seo.overviewTitle: Advanced Spreadsheet & Financial Scenario Modeling (Excel / Sheets)
seo.overviewBody: Spreadsheets remain the most ubiquitous analytical tool in corporate environments. Employers test candidates on advanced lookup functions (XLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH), dynamic array formulas, Pivot Tables, and scenario modeling (Goal Seek, Data Tables).

deliverables.title: 1. Financial Scenario Spreadsheet Model
deliverables.desc: Excel workbook (.xlsx) featuring dynamic scenario inputs, sensitivity tables, and automated financial statements.

deliverables.title: 2. Pivot Table & Summary Dashboard
deliverables.desc: Interactive Pivot Table summary displaying multi-dimensional aggregation views.

deliverables.title: 3. Model User Guide & Formula Audit
deliverables.desc: Documentation explaining model assumptions, formula structures, and error-checking controls.

faqs.question: Why is XLOOKUP superior to VLOOKUP in Excel?
faqs.answer: XLOOKUP searches in any direction (left or right), defaults to exact matching, handles column insertions safely, and does not require static column index numbers.

faqs.question: What is the function of INDEX/MATCH?
faqs.answer: INDEX returns a value from a specified cell range based on row/column numbers, while MATCH searches for a value and returns its position, offering flexible 2D lookups.

faqs.question: How do you prevent spreadsheet formula corruption?
faqs.answer: Use named ranges, lock calculation inputs, apply cell protection, and separate raw data tabs from calculation tabs.
